topic: Biology — The development of understanding of genetics and evolution
subject: combined-science

items.q: Which observation is evidence that supports the theory of evolution by natural selection?
items.correct: Antibiotic resistance evolves in bacterial populations.
items.misconception: Dead organisms are turned into fossils in the rocks.
items.why: Museums and textbooks show large numbers of fossils, so fossilisation looks like the normal fate of a dead organism rather than a rare event. Fossils are the 'remains' of organisms from millions of years ago, which are found in rocks. Fossils may be formed from parts of organisms that have not decayed because one or more of the conditions needed for decay are absent, when parts of the organism are replaced by minerals as they decay, or as preserved traces of organisms.
items.random_wrong: Animals that exercise pass strength to their young.

items.q: Which statement about how fossils are formed is correct?
items.correct: Traces of footprints and burrows are preserved.
items.misconception: Bones and shells are kept, but footprints are not.
items.why: The word 'remains' is read as body parts, and the fossils on display in museums are usually skeletons, so traces are not recognised as fossils. Fossils may be formed as preserved traces of organisms, such as footprints, burrows and rootlet traces, as well as from parts that have not decayed and from parts replaced by minerals as they decay.
items.random_wrong: A dead organism will turn into a fossil in the rock.

items.q: Why can scientists not be certain about how life began on Earth?
items.correct: Early life was soft-bodied and so left few traces.
items.misconception: Scientists have now collected all the earliest fossils.
items.why: Evolutionary trees are drawn as complete, unbroken branching diagrams, which gives the impression that the fossil record has no gaps in it. Many early forms of life were soft-bodied, which means that they have left few traces behind. What traces there were have been mainly destroyed by geological activity. This is why scientists cannot be certain about how life began on Earth.
items.random_wrong: Early organisms had bones which dissolved in rocks.

items.q: An evolutionary tree shows species P and Q meeting at a branch point, with species R branching off much earlier. What does the tree show?
items.correct: P and Q share a more recent common ancestor than R.
items.misconception: Species Q evolved directly from species P.
items.why: Trees are read like a family tree of parents and children, so a species drawn next to or below another is taken to be its ancestor. An evolutionary tree lets us learn how much or how little different organisms have changed as life developed on Earth. A branch point represents an ancestor shared by the organisms on the branches above it, not one present-day species descending from another.
items.random_wrong: P and Q are separate species as they look different.

items.q: A species of bird disappears from Earth after a volcanic eruption destroys its habitat. Which statement is correct?
items.correct: A catastrophic event can cause a species to die out.
items.misconception: The species is extinct once its numbers fall very low.
items.why: News reports use 'extinct' and 'endangered' loosely and often interchangeably, so the two words become blurred. Extinctions occur when there are no remaining individuals of a species still alive.
items.random_wrong: Human hunting is what makes a species become extinct.

items.q: A patient's MRSA infection is not killed by an antibiotic. Why has the population of the resistant strain risen?
items.correct: Resistant bacteria survived and then reproduced very rapidly.
items.misconception: The antibiotic changed the bacteria so they resist it.
items.why: Resistance is noticed after antibiotics have been used, so the antibiotic is taken to be the cause of the change rather than the thing selecting between strains that already differ. Mutations of bacterial pathogens produce new strains. Some strains might be resistant to antibiotics, and so are not killed. They survive and reproduce, so the population of the resistant strain rises. Bacteria can evolve rapidly because they reproduce at a fast rate.
items.random_wrong: The bacteria needed to resist, so they became resistant.

items.q: Which action would reduce the rate of development of antibiotic resistant strains?
items.why: Antibiotics are the most familiar prescribed medicine for feeling ill, and patients often expect them whatever the cause of the illness. To reduce the rate of development of antibiotic resistant strains, doctors should not prescribe antibiotics inappropriately, such as treating non-serious or viral infections.
items.random_wrong: Stopping a course of antibiotics when symptoms go.

items.q: A population of mice lives in a cold place. Over many generations the mice come to have thicker fur. How does this happen?
items.correct: Mice that already had thicker fur were more likely to survive to breed successfully, so the characteristic was passed on to the next generation.
items.misconception: Each mouse grows thicker fur during its own lifetime because of the cold, and then passes that thicker fur on to its offspring.
items.why: Lamarck's idea matches everyday experience of bodies responding to their surroundings, such as muscles growing with use, and it feels more purposeful and tidier than selection acting on variation that is already there. Other theories, including that of Jean-Baptiste Lamarck, are based mainly on the idea that changes that occur in an organism during its lifetime can be inherited. We now know that in the vast majority of cases this type of inheritance cannot occur. Individuals with characteristics most suited to the environment are more likely to survive to breed successfully, and it is those characteristics that are then passed on to the next generation.

items.q: Why do plants growing in a dry habitat have deeper roots than related plants in a wet habitat?
items.correct: Individuals with deeper roots were more likely to survive to breed successfully, so this characteristic was passed on to the next generation.
items.misconception: The plants needed more water, so they made themselves grow deeper roots; evolution gives organisms the characteristics they need.
items.why: Everyday language such as 'the plant adapted to reach water' suggests organisms change on purpose, so students give the process an aim that it does not have. Evolution by natural selection has no aim. Individual organisms within a particular species show a wide range of variation for a characteristic, and individuals with characteristics most suited to the environment are more likely to survive to breed successfully.
items.note: no MCQ covers this misconception, so no third distractor was authored for it; none invented

items.q: Two isolated populations of one species now look noticeably different. Are they two species?
items.correct: Not necessarily. They are two species only once they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.
items.misconception: As soon as two groups of organisms look clearly different from each other they are two separate species.
items.why: Species are usually introduced to students through pictures and appearance, so looking different is taken as the test for being a different species. Populations become isolated and experience different conditions, and natural selection selects different characteristics in each population. Over many generations the two populations become so different that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring. Alfred Wallace did much pioneering work on speciation but more evidence over time has led to our current understanding of the theory of speciation.

items.q: Which factors may contribute to the extinction of a species?
items.correct: Changes to the environment over geological time, new predators, new diseases, new more successful competitors, or a single catastrophic event.
items.misconception: Species only become extinct because of human activity such as hunting or clearing habitats.
items.why: Almost every extinction reported in the media today is caused by people, so other causes acting over geological time are overlooked. Factors which may contribute to the extinction of a species include changes to the environment over geological time, new predators, new diseases, new more successful competitors, and a single catastrophic event such as a massive volcanic eruption or a collision with an asteroid.

items.q: Why should a patient complete a course of antibiotics?
items.correct: So that all bacteria are killed and none survive to mutate and form resistant strains.
items.misconception: Once the symptoms have gone the infection is over, so the rest of the tablets are not needed.
items.why: Feeling better is taken as proof that every bacterium has already been killed, so the remaining doses seem pointless. Patients should complete their course of antibiotics so all bacteria are killed and none survive to mutate and form resistant strains.

items.q: Can developing new antibiotics solve the problem of resistance on its own?
items.correct: No. The development of new antibiotics is costly and slow and is unlikely to keep up with the emergence of new resistant strains.
items.misconception: Scientists can simply develop a new antibiotic whenever a resistant strain appears.
items.why: New medicines are reported as sudden breakthroughs, which hides the cost and the many years of development behind them. The development of new antibiotics is costly and slow. It is unlikely to keep up with the emergence of new resistant strains, so the use of antibiotics must also be controlled.
